backbone: Build a group from Osajda-labelled expanders as graphical relators, construct a local operator with uniform spectral gap whose kernel projection has irrational trace; Lück's rational-trace theorem blocks surjectivity.
quote: Thus a projection in \(C_r^*(G)\) with irrational trace would obstruct surjectivity. We construct such a projection.

backbone: Reduce to a weakly mixing lattice setting, build commuting boundary-map projection-valued measures from flag-space measurements, and extract a finite invariant partition whose stabilizers give subgroup isomorphisms and projective fibres.
quote: In this reduced setting the goal is a fixed orthogonal partition of the correspondence $K$ into finite-dimensional subspaces, permuted by both endpoint groups, with free actions and finitely many orbits.

backbone: Inductively perturb freely generating Haar tuples of L(F_{n+1}) by trace-preserving polynomial flows with norm control; the limit tuple shows L(F_n)≅L(F_{n+1}), and amplification reaches rank two.
quote: We construct freely generating Haar tuples $(A^{(k)},C^{(k)})$ and positive numbers $r_k$ by induction.

backbone: Prove a uniform commutator estimate for all matrix amplifications of inner derivations (finite factors via free products and Popa independence, then central decomposition); Paulsen and Kirchberg's equivalence then give similarity.
quote: Their scalar commutator norms are uniformly bounded, so \eqref{eq:universal} gives complete boundedness of the full derivation. Paulsen's theorem implements it, and Kirchberg's equivalence proves Theorem~\ref{thm:similarity}.

backbone: Finite factors: uniform commutator amplification plus amenable-cocycle averaging give a near-identity isomorphism; then infinite factors via modular alignment and crossed products, then centers; small unitaries implement these isomorphisms.
quote: Transporting this isomorphism back and applying the commutator estimate gives a small unitary on the original Hilbert space.

backbone: Existing criteria reduce to a core fixed-point equality; the multiplication identity R=L·exp(iX⊗Y), obtained from the absolute bicentralizer theorem and repeated tensor tests (each by contradiction), yields the commutation.
quote: Existing bicentralizer criteria reduce our task to showing that the extension of $\gamma$ to $B\rtimes_{\sigma^\varphi}\R$ has fixed algebra $N'\cap c(M)$.

backbone: Verify equivariant uniform property Gamma, then apply Szabó–Wouters absorption, by building commuting orbit rows in the central sequence algebra, Gaussian quadratics over Følner sets, a weighted Haar unitary and equal-trace projections.
quote: If the action has equivariant uniform property Gamma, it is cocycle conjugate to its tensor product with the trivial action on \(\Zalg\).

backbone: For the explicit group Z[1/2]^3⋊(SL_3(Z)×Z), a representation inequivalent to its pullbacks plus a Kazhdan spectral test show an ultrapower embedding forces finite predecessor chains, hence periodicity: contradiction.
quote: We construct a finite-dimensional representation inequivalent to each of its positive pullbacks along a fixed group endomorphism.

backbone: Construct an explicit 2-adic measurable field of weighted shifts with quadratic log-weights and a bounded commuting backward intertwiner; Domar-type support separation classifies fibre invariant subspaces, leaving no hyperinvariant subspace.
quote: We give a negative answer to the hyperinvariant-subspace problem by constructing, on every infinite-dimensional separable complex Hilbert space, a nonzero bounded norm-quasinilpotent operator with no nonzero proper closed hyperinvariant subspace.

backbone: Build a separable algebra from shifts on sums of vector bundles whose Chern classes survive while normalized bundle maps expand subspaces; no matrix amplification is properly infinite, yet a fixed pair has defect 1/144.
quote: We construct such an algebra and obtain a fixed positive pair witnessing nonadditivity.

backbone: Reduce to separable type II1; construct a unitary random walk with asymptotically free products, prove a Liouville theorem for harmonic maps via martingales and free-word rigidity, then average the last cocycle input.
quote: We obtain the needed module identity by averaging over a single unitary random walk.

backbone: Relative generators form a G-delta; Baire gives continuity points of projection norms, and a Popa-independence perturbation along long words shows W*(P,u) cannot be proper there, so generators are dense.
quote: Baire's theorem supplies common continuity points for a countable dense family of vectors, and contractivity extends continuity to every vector.

backbone: Transfinite recursion of length c^+ adjoins reduced HNN unitaries joining pairs of pure-state classes while preserving unique state extensions; countable determination ensures every pair of pure states is eventually joined.
quote: We start with a separable simple algebra, adjoin one unitary at each active successor stage, and take norm closures of unions at limits.

backbone: Construct a tuple with sparse higher cumulants and block structure; a cumulant Fisher-information bound keeps χ* near semicircular, while a persistent block-structure entropy deficit of noisy microstates keeps χ lower.
quote: We construct a bounded self-adjoint tuple $X$ in a von Neumann algebra with faithful normal tracial state such that $-\infty<\chi(X)\leq\chi^*(X)-\tfrac12<\infty$.

backbone: Without characters, a finite tensor power carries a matrix-cone homomorphism with full corner from representation-independent tensor labels; a stable-rank-free Rørdam–Winter criterion upgrades it to a dimension-drop map, embedding Z centrally.
quote: This is the input to the stable-rank-free implication of R\o rdam and Winter \cite[Proposition~5.1, (ii)$\Rightarrow$(iv)]{RW}, whose needed form is proved explicitly in Section~\ref{sec:rw}.

backbone: Reduce to a faithful central state; on the normalizer part build a random Bernoulli coloring via mixed determinantal polynomials and sparse iterative pinning; off it use random diagonal unitaries and free moments.
quote: We construct a measurable coloring there that has uniform conditional color marginals and makes the pinched matrix small on any prescribed finite-radius ball with arbitrarily high probability.

backbone: Transport the cone isomorphism to Cuntz semigroups; build sequence-algebra models realizing traces with ideal-wise error control, prove norm uniqueness, correct the models, and conclude by approximate intertwining.
quote: The existence, uniqueness, and approximate-intertwining organization of those classification arguments also provides the broad method used here, with new local estimates needed for arbitrary ideals.

backbone: Assume a finite cover has rate exceeding twice the comparison radius; comparison along orbit blocks yields a bundle embedding, and cobordism-based torus compression with colored packets lowers covering order, contradicting the rate.
quote: Suppose, to the contrary, that a cover has rate $d>2r$.

backbone: Graph measurements of orthogonal copies reduce failure to finitely many explicit equalities, excluded by a four-entry contradiction under proper infiniteness; cutoffs and iteration give arbitrary-entry diagonalization, hence strong pure infiniteness.
quote: A graph of orthogonal copies first turns possible failure into finitely many explicit equalities. Once those equalities have been excluded, ideal cutoffs convert the resulting nonvanishing into one global support estimate.

backbone: Reduce to excluding faithful Z_p actions; such an action yields p^k equal integral sheaf-Witt signature classes summing to 4u_d in a group whose rational image lies in a fixed lattice: contradiction.
quote: A faithful \(\Zp\)-action will produce, for every \(k\geq1\), \(p^k\) integral classes in this group. Their rational images are equal and sum to \(4\overline{u}_d\).

backbone: Construct an explicit 4-manifold with immersed discs and framed algebraic duals; hypothetical disjoint locally flat discs would give formal Chern–Simons deformation data, which a Frobenius–Koszul tensor obstruction rules out.
quote: We construct a compact oriented smooth four-manifold containing finitely many disc maps with framed algebraic dual spheres whose boundary circles bound no disjoint locally flat discs.

backbone: Prior work reduces to genus two with slopes ±2; for such a pair, a nonzero instanton count Ω and a one-dimensional nonabelian-monopole spinor count whose boundary forces 2^η·Ω=0 contradict each other.
quote: There are two counts. The first is an integer instanton count $\Omega\ne0$ on a closed parameterized cobordism. The second is an oriented one-dimensional spinor count whose boundary would force $2^\eta\Omega=0$.

backbone: Construct congruence-fibre graphs over discrete tori with two torus ends; a winding class persists at every Rips scale, while a property-(T) transfer in the maximal Roe algebra moves its index to the ends, where it cancels.
quote: We construct a graph with two torus ends and a long central region of constant fiber size.

backbone: In an ultraproduct-over-primes category, inductively form Y_{j+1} as cofibres of classes b_j from uniformly localized permutation powers, detect them by a cobordism coefficient identity, then descend to one prime.
quote: We construct objects $Y_0,\ldots,Y_{n+1}$ in $\cC$, starting from $Y_0=\one$, and, for $0\leq j\leq n$, maps

backbone: Indices 0,1,2 are classical; every j≥4 is excluded since its nonzero image in the height-six C_9 detector must support an outgoing differential; the stem-322 class is built by Toda's extended-cube construction.
quote: Theorem~\ref{cube:order-three}, proved in Section~\ref{sec:cube} using the finite algebra of Section~\ref{sec:finite}, constructs an exact-order-three representative detected by $b_3$. These assertions exhaust all nonnegative indices.

backbone: Take a minimal counterexample; established reductions force a Lie-type simple component; for each classical family, frame-built decorated rational cycles with nonzero coefficients propagate to G, contradicting vanishing homology.
quote: Let $G$ be a minimal-order counterexample to \eqref{eq:HQC} for $p=2$.

backbone: Nonzero analytic germs on height strata cannot vanish on stabilizer orbits (Tate-basis coordinates, Frobenius-power identity, Fargues–Fontaine nondegeneracy), so invariant primes are exactly I_h; Barthel–Heard–Naumann yields Hovey–Strickland.
quote: We prove both classifications, using the arithmetic problem as the main step.

backbone: Show elementary expansions are weak equivalences using an exact-boundary weak-equivalence test, contractible tree shapes, and partial cylinders interpreting each coherator operation; Henry's comparison then yields equivalence with spaces.
quote: The source endpoint is a weak equivalence by Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, and hence so is the last map.

backbone: Prove finiteness of continuous stabilizer cohomology for a broad coefficient class via p-adic geometry (Fargues–Fontaine towers, Kummer supports, Laurent models) with uniform vanishing; descent then gives degreewise finite generation.
quote: Fix a height $n$ formal group over a sufficiently large finite field $\kk$ of characteristic $p$. Let $E_n$ be its Morava $E$-theory and let $P_n$ be its ordinary stabilizer group. The algebraic conclusion that drives the proof is

backbone: Cyclic chains give the upper bound; for the lower bound, rational estimates from maximizing pro-p towers and subgroup congruences, glued across heights, force at a minimal failing height a support splitting contradicting irreducibility.
quote: At a least height where the proposed bound fails, the estimates isolate the offending subgroup component from the other components.

backbone: Assume b_1^(2)>0; a finite-energy function yields a compact boundary with convergence dynamics; cut-point trees and annular path-pushing make it a locally connected continuum, contradicting the dimension and cohomology constraints.
quote: Suppose the first $L^2$-Betti number is positive.
